chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding two sisters who were presented to two brothers on one night, and the wife of this one was brought to this one and the wife of that one was brought to that one, he said: 'For each of them, the dowry is due upon consummation (ghishyan). And if their guardian intentionally did that, he is fined the dowry, and one of them does not approach his wife until the waiting period (iddah) expires. When the waiting period expires, each of them returns to her husband by the first marriage.' It was said to him: 'If they died before the expiration of the waiting period?' He said: 'The two husbands return with half the dowry upon their heirs, and the two men inherit them.' It was said: 'If the two men died while they were in the waiting period?' He said: 'They inherit them, and for them is half of the specified dowry, and upon them is the waiting period. After they finish from the first waiting period, they observe the waiting period of the one whose wife died.'.

key_terms.التَّدْلِيس: Deception or mixing up (in the context of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences and inheritance rules when two sisters are married to two brothers but are mixed up during the wedding night?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fiqh of *tadlis* (confusion/mix-up) in marriage consummation, establishing that each brother retains the dowry (*sadaq*) associated with his specific act of intimacy while the marriage contract remains valid with the original spouse. It further clarifies inheritance dynamics, noting that if death occurs during the waiting period (*iddah*), the brothers inherit from the sisters as if the marriage were fully consummated, a ruling grounded in the principle that *iddah* serves as a continuation of marital ties. This case highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the distinction between the contract (*aqd*) and consummation (*dukhul*) in determining financial and inheritance rights.
